title: Intruder Alarm MONSTER
tagline: Protect your secret base with an ultrasonic security tripwire and alarm!

phases.instructions: Locate these parts from your kit: Arduino Uno, HC-SR04 Ultrasonic Distance Sensor, Piezo Buzzer, Red LED, 220-ohm resistor, and jumper wires.
verificationCheckpoints: Arduino Uno and USB-B cable ready
HC-SR04 sensor pins are straight and clean
Peel off yellow paper sticker from top of buzzer

phases.instructions: Mount the HC-SR04 sensor and Buzzer onto your breadboard. Follow the color-coded connections below to hook up power, ground, echo timing, and buzzer triggers.
verificationCheckpoints: GND wires connected to Dark Slate GND rail
TRIG is in Pin 9 and ECHO is in Pin 10
Resistor is in series with LED anode

phases.instructions: SAFETY FIRST! Never plug in your board until you complete this pre-flight verification checklist. A short between 5V and GND can harm your board.
verificationCheckpoints: Unplug USB cable during physical inspection
Confirm Red wire connects to 5V and Dark Slate wire connects to GND
Ensure no bare component legs touch each other
Verify buzzer polarity: (+) pin connects to Pin 8

phases.instructions: Review how the Arduino pulses the ultrasonic speaker and calculates echo roundtrip time into distance in centimeters.
phases.codeExplanation:
- TRIG_PIN emits a 10-microsecond ultrasonic chirp at 40 kHz.
- pulseIn(ECHO_PIN, HIGH) measures how many microseconds elapsed before the echo bounced back.
- Multiplying by sound speed (0.0343 cm/us) and dividing by 2 yields distance to obstacle.
- If obstacle < 30cm, the alarm sounds tone(2000Hz) and illuminates the LED.
verificationCheckpoints: Understand how pulseIn measures travel time
Understand why dividing by 2 is necessary (out-and-back trip)

phases.instructions: Connect USB cable to your computer, compile and upload the sketch. Wave your hand toward the sensor to verify perimeter tripwire triggering.
verificationCheckpoints: Hand at 50cm: buzzer quiet, LED dark
Hand moves closer than 30cm: buzzer chirps, LED flashes
Serial monitor displays live distance readings in cm

phases.instructions: Awesome job! You successfully built and tested an active ultrasonic perimeter detector. Position it near your bedroom door or desk to guard against intruders!
verificationCheckpoints: Ready to claim Security Rookie badge

troubleshooting.cause: TRIG and ECHO pins are swapped
troubleshooting.solution: Swap pins 9 and 10 on your breadboard or verify wires.
diagnosticSteps: Check TRIG on Pin 9 and ECHO on Pin 10.
Verify acoustic line of sight is clear.

troubleshooting.symptom: Buzzer clicks faintly but makes no siren
troubleshooting.cause: Buzzer protective sticker not removed or negative pin on wrong rail
troubleshooting.solution: Peel off the round yellow label and ensure (-) pin is in the GND rail.
diagnosticSteps: Peel off the yellow protective sticker on top.
Ensure longer (+) pin is connected to Pin 8 and (-) to GND.

troubleshooting.solution: Unplug LED and rotate 180 degrees. The longer leg (anode) must connect toward Pin 7.
diagnosticSteps: Rotate LED 180 degrees to verify polarity.
Check that 220Ω resistor connects cathode to GND.

variants.title: Dual Piezo Stereo Siren
variants.description: Use two piezos on separate pins with alternating frequencies to create an authentic European police siren effect.
variants.wiringDifferences: Connect second buzzer to Pin 6 and GND
variants.codeAdaptation: Alternate tone(8, 800) and tone(6, 600) with 250ms intervals

extensionMissions.title: Stealth Silent Alarm
extensionMissions.objective: Silence the loud piezo and replace it with an invisible infrared beacon or silent strobe warning to catch intruders unawares.
hints: Replace tone() with digitalWrite() pulsing on an LED or IR LED pin
Ensure the loop still calculates distance accurately

story: A pesky shadow monster is sneaking into your laboratory while you sleep! Build an automated ultrasonic radar sentry tripwire that monitors room distance and sounds a loud piezo siren whenever an intruder breaches the 30cm perimeter.
